description: Rotate any image in 90° steps and flip it horizontally or vertically, with a live preview of every change. Download the transformed image as a PNG in one click.

faq.a: Rotating by 90° steps is lossless in terms of scaling — no resizing happens, the pixels are simply rearranged.
Yes — flips and rotations stack. Use Reset to return to the original orientation.
faq.q: Can I combine rotation and flipping?

faq.a: No — all transformations run locally in your browser via canvas.

howTo: Upload an image.
Rotate left/right or toggle horizontal/vertical flips — the preview updates live.
Click Download PNG to save the result.
name: Image Rotate & Flip
tagline: Rotate 90° and flip images with live preview

description: Apply photo filters like grayscale, sepia and invert, or fine-tune blur, brightness, contrast and saturation with sliders. Compare before and after side by side, then download the filtered PNG.

faq.a: Each preset is just a combination of slider values — after applying one you can still adjust every slider yourself.
The image is rendered at its full original resolution before filters are applied.
Yes — filtering uses the canvas API in your browser, no network needed.

howTo: Upload an image.
Pick a preset or adjust the individual sliders.
Switch between After and Before to compare.
Download the filtered PNG.
name: Image Filters
tagline: Grayscale, sepia, invert and fine-tuned adjustments

description: Turn any image into a Base64 data URI you can paste straight into HTML, CSS or code. See the original size, the encoded length and the size overhead, then copy or download the result.

faq.a: Base64 encoding adds about 33% overhead — small icons are the best use case.
faq.q: Why is the output bigger than the image?

faq.a: Yes — paste the data URI directly into the src attribute of an img tag.
faq.q: Can I use the result in an tag?

faq.a: No — encoding happens entirely on your device.

howTo: Upload an image.
The Base64 data URI is generated instantly.
Copy it to the clipboard or download it as a .txt file.
name: Image to Base64
tagline: Convert images to Base64 data URIs

description: Paste a Base64 data URI or raw Base64 payload to preview the image it contains. The tool validates the input and lets you download the decoded image as a PNG.

faq.a: No — if you paste only the raw Base64, PNG is assumed automatically.
faq.q: Do I need the data:image/png;base64, prefix?

faq.a: The string may be truncated or contain characters outside the Base64 alphabet. Copy the full value and retry.
faq.q: Why does it say my string is invalid?

faq.a: No — decoding and previewing happen locally in your browser.
faq.q: Is the decoded data sent anywhere?

howTo: Paste your Base64 string (with or without the data: prefix).
Click Preview image.
Download the result as PNG.
name: Base64 to Image
tagline: Decode Base64 strings back into images

description: Upload a logo or image and get perfectly sized favicon PNGs at 16×16, 32×32 and 180×180. Download each size individually or grab them all at once.

faq.a: Use 16×16 and 32×32 for the browser tab favicon, and 180×180 as the Apple touch icon.
Square images give the best results — the tool scales your image to fit each size.
faq.q: Should my source image be square?

faq.a: No — rendering happens on your device with the canvas API.

howTo: Upload your logo or a square image.
Favicons are generated instantly at all three sizes.
Download each PNG or click Download all.

name: Favicon Generator
tagline: Create 16, 32 and 180px favicons from any image

description: Add classic meme-style top and bottom captions to any image, with bold outlined text and adjustable font size. Preview your meme live and download it as a PNG.

faq.a: Yes — any image you upload works as a meme background.
faq.q: Can I use my own photos?

faq.a: Yes — long captions wrap onto multiple lines so they always fit the image.
No — the meme is rendered locally in your browser.

howTo: Upload a background image.
Type your top and bottom captions.
Adjust the font size and toggle uppercase.
Download your meme as PNG.
name: Meme Generator
tagline: Classic top/bottom captions with outline text

description: Give any image smooth rounded corners and export it as a transparent PNG. Add an optional coloured border with adjustable width for avatars and cards.

faq.a: PNG supports transparency, so the corners outside the rounded shape stay see-through. JPG cannot do that.
faq.q: Why is the download a PNG?

faq.a: Yes — set the radius to half the smaller side of a square image.
faq.q: Can I make a perfect circle?

faq.a: No — everything runs locally on your device.

howTo: Upload an image.
Drag the corner-radius slider to round the edges.
Optionally add a coloured border.
Download the transparent PNG.
name: Rounded Corners
tagline: Round image corners with optional border

description: Paste raw SVG markup or upload an .svg file and rasterize it to a crisp PNG at any dimensions you choose. Perfect for turning vector logos into fixed-size images.

faq.a: Yes — SVG is vector, so rendering at larger dimensions produces crisp results at any size.
Yes — transparent areas of the SVG stay transparent in the PNG.
No — rasterization happens entirely in your browser.

howTo: Paste SVG markup or drop an .svg file.
Enter the output width and height.
Click Convert to PNG and download.
name: SVG to PNG
tagline: Rasterize SVG markup at any size

description: Combine four photos into a clean 2×2 collage. Control the gap between photos, the background colour and the cell size, then download the finished collage as a PNG.

faq.a: No — each photo is cropped to fill its square cell automatically.
faq.q: Do all photos need the same size?

faq.a: Yes — empty slots show a placeholder with the slot number.
faq.q: Can I leave a slot empty?

faq.a: No — the collage is assembled locally in your browser.

howTo: Drop a photo into each of the four slots.
Adjust the gap, background colour and cell size.
Download the collage PNG.
iconSvg: <rect x="3" y="3" width="18" height="18" rx="2"/><path d="M12 3v18M3 12h18"/>
name: Photo Collage

description: Click anywhere on an uploaded image to sample that pixel's exact colour. See the HEX and RGB values, copy them with one click, and build a palette history of every colour you pick.

faq.a: Pixel-perfect — it reads the exact RGB value from the full-resolution image, not the scaled preview.
faq.q: How accurate is the sampled colour?

faq.a: The last 12 sampled colours are kept; click any swatch to copy it again.
faq.q: How many colours does the palette keep?

faq.a: No — colour sampling happens entirely on your device.

howTo: Upload an image.
Click any point on it to sample the colour.
Copy the HEX or RGB value.
Click palette swatches to re-copy earlier colours.
name: Image Eyedropper
tagline: Pick colours from any image, keep a palette

description: Convert any photo into ASCII art rendered in plain characters. Adjust the width and character set, invert for dark backgrounds, then copy the art or download it as a .txt file.

faq.a: High-contrast photos with a clear subject — portraits and bold shapes render best.
ASCII art needs a monospace font so every character is the same width — the preview uses one automatically.
faq.q: Why does it look wrong in some fonts?

faq.a: No — conversion runs locally in your browser.

howTo: Upload a photo.
Set the character width and pick a character set.
Copy the ASCII art or download it as .txt.
name: Image to ASCII Art
